subject: basic-computing
title: Introduction to Social Networking
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: What is LinkedIn?
questions.answer: A business and employment-oriented social networking platform that helps prepare a professional profile and find jobs.

questions.q: Who created Facebook?
questions.answer: Mark Zuckerberg.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of characters in a tweet?
questions.answer: 280 characters.

questions.q: What is a hashtag?
questions.answer: A keyword preceded by # that connects a tweet to a general topic.

questions.q: Who is a blogger?
questions.answer: A person who frequently writes a blog.

questions.q: What is a vlog?
questions.answer: A video blog, i.e. a blog containing video material.

questions.q: What is a digital footprint?
questions.answer: The trail of information a user leaves behind after using the internet.

questions.q: Name the two types of digital footprints.
questions.answer: Passive and active digital footprints.

questions.q: Which social site is business and employment oriented?
questions.answer: LinkedIn.

questions.q: What does subscribing to a YouTube channel do?
questions.answer: It makes the channel send notifications whenever a new video is uploaded.

questions.q: What is stealing someone else's identity online called in the textbook?
questions.answer: Hacking.

questions.q: Name any two social networking sites.
questions.answer: Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, YouTube (any two).

questions.q: Write the URL used to create a blog in the lesson.
questions.answer: www.blogger.com.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is LinkedIn? How can you proceed to search for a job on LinkedIn?
questions.answer: LinkedIn is a professional social networking site for a profile and jobs. Steps: sign in, click the Jobs section or type a job title, location or company in the search bar, select the Jobs tab, apply filters such as Sort by and Date posted, and click Apply.

questions.q: Define social networking. What are its advantages in the field of education?
questions.answer: Social networking is linking with friends, family and others on the web to share information. In education students and teachers can learn from experts at any time and place, free or paid.

questions.q: Define the following: (i) Social Networking (ii) Blog (iii) Digital footprints (any two for 2 marks).
questions.answer: (i) Social networking: linking and sharing with people through websites or apps. (ii) Blog: an online diary or journal website. (iii) Digital footprint: the trail of data left after using the internet.

questions.q: Differentiate between Twitter and Tweet.
questions.answer: Twitter is the microblogging social networking service; a tweet is a short post of up to 280 characters made on it.

questions.q: Differentiate between Blog and Blogger.
questions.answer: A blog is a website like a diary; a blogger is the person who writes the blog.

questions.q: Differentiate between Facebook and LinkedIn.
questions.answer: Facebook is for personal connections, sharing photos and posts with friends; LinkedIn is professional networking for jobs and career profiles.

questions.q: Explain the disadvantages of social media.
questions.answer: Hacking and fake identity, frauds through harmful links, cyber bullying, and addiction with health problems.

questions.q: Explain the various types of digital footprints.
questions.answer: Passive footprint: data collected without the knowledge of the user. Active footprint: data released deliberately by the user, e.g. posts on social media.

questions.q: How can the digital trail be reduced? Give any four ways.
questions.answer: Check privacy settings, remove old accounts, unsubscribe from mailing lists, use stealth browsing, think before posting, use anti-tracking tools.

questions.q: What is the importance of social media?
questions.answer: It connects people, gives real-time updates, supports education and marketing and creates awareness about causes.

questions.q: Write the steps to create a blog on Blogger.
questions.answer: Go to www.blogger.com, click Create your blog, sign in with Gmail, click Create New Blog, enter title, address and template, click New post, write and click Publish.

questions.q: How can you add a friend on Facebook?
questions.answer: Click the search bar, type the friend's name, select the profile and click Add Friend; the friend must accept the request.

questions.q: Write the steps to post a tweet.
questions.answer: Log in to Twitter, type the message in the What's happening box (add a photo, GIF or video if needed) and click Tweet.

questions.q: What are the options for the audience while sharing a Facebook post?
questions.answer: Public, Friends, Friends except, Specific friends and Only me.

sections.title: Answer the questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any three disadvantages of social networking.
questions.answer: Hacking or fake identities can harm people; fraud through harmful links and sharing of personal information; cyber bullying causes depression; addiction harms health (any three, with explanation).

questions.q: Explain the advantages of social networking.
questions.answer: Connectivity across the world; real-time updates; education from experts; marketing and online orders; awareness and fund collection for noble causes.

questions.q: Write the steps to create an account on LinkedIn and make it secure.
questions.answer: Open www.linkedin.com, enter details to create the account, sign in, update academic details under edit profile, click Me, Settings and Privacy, and change Login and security.

questions.q: Explain how to make a Facebook account secure.
questions.answer: Open Settings, Security and Login; enable two-factor authentication; set privacy so only friends see details; use Manage Blocking to block unwanted apps and users.

questions.q: Explain Twitter, tweets, hashtags and following.
questions.answer: Twitter is a microblogging site where members post tweets up to 280 characters; a hashtag #keyword links a tweet to a topic; anyone can follow anyone with a single click by searching the account.

questions.q: Explain blogs and how to create a blog.
questions.answer: A blog is an online journal written by a blogger; on blogger.com sign in with Gmail, create a new blog with title, address and template, write a new post and Publish; it can be edited and shared.

questions.q: Explain digital footprints and ways to reduce them.
questions.answer: Digital footprints are the information left behind online; passive (collected without knowledge) and active (shared deliberately). Reduce by privacy settings, removing old accounts, unsubscribing, stealth browsing, thinking before posting and anti-tracking tools.
